skills.body:
---
name: baoyu-diagram
description: Create professional diagrams with configurable dark/light theme via CSS custom properties. Use this skill whenever the user asks for any kind of technical or conceptual diagram, visualization of a system, process flow, data flow, component relationship, network topology, decision tree, org chart, state machine, or any visual representation of structure/logic/process. Also trigger when the user says "画个图" "画一个架构图" "diagram" "flowchart" "sequence diagram" "draw me a ..." or uploads content and asks to visualize it. Outputs a dark-theme SVG, a light-theme SVG, and a @2x PNG of each.
version: 1.118.0
---

# Diagram Generator

Create SVG diagrams. Each SVG embeds its own styles, uses CSS custom properties for theming, and loads nothing over the network.

## Output Files

For a diagram saved as `<name>.svg`, produce exactly these files:

| File | What it is | Made by |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `<name>.svg` | Source SVG, CSS variables with dark theme values | You (the LLM) |
| `<name>.light.svg` | Same markup with light theme values | `theme-switch.ts --theme=light` |
| `<name>@2x.png` | Dark PNG at 2x scale | `main.ts` |
| `<name>.light@2x.png` | Light PNG at 2x scale | `main.ts --theme light` |

If the user asks for only one theme, or only SVG, produce just those files.

## Themes

All colors are CSS custom properties defined in the `:root` block of the SVG's `<style>`; markup references them as `var(--bg)`, `var(--color-primary-fill)`, etc. Never hardcode color values in SVG attributes.

Theme values live in `{baseDir}/themes/<name>.json` — one flat JSON object mapping CSS property names (keys starting with `--`) to colors. Other keys (e.g. `"description"`) are metadata, ignored by scripts. Built-in: `dark.json`, `light.json`.

**Custom themes:** drop a new `.json` into `themes/` — no script changes needed:

```json
// themes/my-brand.json
{
  "description": "Corporate brand theme",
  "--bg": "#ffffff",
  "--text": "#1a1a2e",
  "--text-muted": "#6b7280",
  "--arrow": "#9ca3af",
  "--color-primary-fill": "rgba(37,99,235,0.12)",
  "--color-primary-stroke": "#2563eb",
  "--color-secondary-fill": "rgba(22,163,74,0.12)",
  "--color-secondary-stroke": "#16a34a"
}
```

Apply with `--theme=my-brand` (`theme-switch.ts`, `main.ts` and `flatten-vars.ts` all support it). Variables omitted from a custom theme are not replaced. When generating SVGs for a custom theme, use its values in the `:root` block.

### CSS Custom Properties

| Variable | Dark Theme Default | Light Theme Value | Usage |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------|-------|
| `--bg` | `#0f172a` | `#f8fafc` | Page background |
| `--bg-grid` | `#1e293b` | `#e2e8f0` | Grid pattern stroke |
| `--mask` | `#0f172a` | `#f8fafc` | Opaque mask fill (same as --bg) |
| `--text` | `white` | `#0f172a` | Primary text color |
| `--text-muted` | `#94a3b8` | `#475569` | Secondary/sublabel text |
| `--arrow` | `#64748b` | `#64748b` | Arrow/connector lines (unchanged) |
| `--color-primary-fill` | `rgba(8,51,68,0.4)` | `rgba(6,182,212,0.12)` | Frontend, user-facing, inputs |
| `--color-primary-stroke` | `#22d3ee` | `#0891b2` | Primary border |
| `--color-secondary-fill` | `rgba(6,78,59,0.4)` | `rgba(5,150,105,0.12)` | Backend, services, processing |
| `--color-secondary-stroke` | `#34d399` | `#059669` | Secondary border |
| `--color-tertiary-fill` | `rgba(76,29,149,0.4)` | `rgba(124,58,237,0.12)` | Database, storage, persistence |
| `--color-tertiary-stroke` | `#a78bfa` | `#7c3aed` | Tertiary border |
| `--color-accent-fill` | `rgba(120,53,15,0.3)` | `rgba(217,119,6,0.12)` | Cloud, infrastructure, regions |
| `--color-accent-stroke` | `#fbbf24` | `#d97706` | Accent border |
| `--color-alert-fill` | `rgba(136,19,55,0.4)` | `rgba(225,29,72,0.12)` | Security, errors, warnings |
| `--color-alert-stroke` | `#fb7185` | `#e11d48` | Alert border |
| `--color-connector-fill` | `rgba(251,146,60,0.3)` | `rgba(234,88,12,0.12)` | Buses, queues, middleware |
| `--color-connector-stroke` | `#fb923c` | `#ea580c` | Connector border |
| `--color-neutral-fill` | `rgba(30,41,59,0.5)` | `rgba(100,116,139,0.12)` | External, generic, unknown |
| `--color-neutral-stroke` | `#94a3b8` | `#64748b` | Neutral border |
| `--color-highlight-fill` | `rgba(59,130,246,0.3)` | `rgba(59,130,246,0.12)` | Active state, focus, current step |
| `--color-highlight-stroke` | `#60a5fa` | `#3b82f6` | Highlight border |

## Design System

### Typography

Use a locally installed monospace font stack. Do not `@import` web fonts or reference any remote resource: the SVG must render the same offline, and the PNG converter cannot fetch fonts.

```svg
<style>
  text { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', 'SF Mono', 'Cascadia Code', 'Noto Sans Mono', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace; }
</style>
```

Font sizes by role:
- **Title:** 16px, weight 700, fill: `var(--text)`
- **Component name:** 11-12px, weight 600, fill: `var(--text)`
- **Sublabel / description:** 9px, weight 400, fill: `var(--text-muted)`
- **Annotation / note:** 8px, weight 400
- **Tiny label (on arrows):** 7-8px

### Core Visual Elements

**Background + Grid:**

```svg
<defs>
  <pattern id="grid" width="40" height="40" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
    <path d="M 40 0 L 0 0 0 40" fill="none" stroke="var(--bg-grid)" stroke-width="0.5"/>
  </pattern>
</defs>
<rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="var(--bg)"/>
<rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="url(#grid)"/>
```

**Arrowhead marker (standard):**

```svg
<marker id="arrow" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
  <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" fill="var(--arrow)"/>
</marker>
```

**Arrowhead marker (colored) — create per-color as needed:**

```svg
<marker id="arrow-primary" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
  <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" fill="var(--color-primary-stroke)"/>
</marker>
```

**Open arrowhead (for async/return messages):**

```svg
<marker id="arrow-open" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
  <polyline points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" fill="none" stroke="var(--arrow)" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</marker>
```

### SVG Structure & Layering

Draw in this order (SVG paints back-to-front):

1. Background fill + grid pattern
2. Region/group boundaries (dashed outlines)
3. Connection arrows and lines
4. Opaque masking rects (same position as component boxes, `fill="var(--mask)"`)
5. Component boxes (semi-transparent fill + stroke via CSS variables)
6. Text labels

# Diagram Generator

Create SVG diagrams. Each SVG embeds its own styles, uses CSS custom properties for theming, and loads nothing over the network.

## Output Files

For a diagram saved as `<name>.svg`, produce exactly these files:

| File | What it is | Made by |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `<name>.svg` | Source SVG, CSS variables with dark theme values | You (the LLM) |
| `<name>.light.svg` | Same markup with light theme values | `theme-switch.ts --theme=light` |
| `<name>@2x.png` | Dark PNG at 2x scale | `main.ts` |
| `<name>.light@2x.png` | Light PNG at 2x scale | `main.ts --theme light` |

If the user asks for only one theme, or only SVG, produce just those files.

## Themes

All colors are CSS custom properties defined in the `:root` block of the SVG's `<style>`; markup references them as `var(--bg)`, `var(--color-primary-fill)`, etc. Never hardcode color values in SVG attributes.

Theme values live in `{baseDir}/themes/<name>.json` — one flat JSON object mapping CSS property names (keys starting with `--`) to colors. Other keys (e.g. `"description"`) are metadata, ignored by scripts. Built-in: `dark.json`, `light.json`.

**Custom themes:** drop a new `.json` into `themes/` — no script changes needed:

```json
// themes/my-brand.json
{
  "description": "Corporate brand theme",
  "--bg": "#ffffff",
  "--text": "#1a1a2e",
  "--text-muted": "#6b7280",
  "--arrow": "#9ca3af",
  "--color-primary-fill": "rgba(37,99,235,0.12)",
  "--color-primary-stroke": "#2563eb",
  "--color-secondary-fill": "rgba(22,163,74,0.12)",
  "--color-secondary-stroke": "#16a34a"
}
```

Apply with `--theme=my-brand` (`theme-switch.ts`, `main.ts` and `flatten-vars.ts` all support it). Variables omitted from a custom theme are not replaced. When generating SVGs for a custom theme, use its values in the `:root` block.

| `--bg-grid` | `#1e293b` | `#e2e8f0` | Grid pattern stroke |
| `--mask` | `#0f172a` | `#f8fafc` | Opaque mask fill (same as --bg) |
| `--text` | `white` | `#0f172a` | Primary text color |
| `--text-muted` | `#94a3b8` | `#475569` | Secondary/sublabel text |
| `--arrow` | `#64748b` | `#64748b` | Arrow/connector lines (unchanged) |

| `--color-tertiary-fill` | `rgba(76,29,149,0.4)` | `rgba(124,58,237,0.12)` | Database, storage, persistence |

| `--color-accent-fill` | `rgba(120,53,15,0.3)` | `rgba(217,119,6,0.12)` | Cloud, infrastructure, regions |

It fails if the SVG references a variable that neither the theme nor the SVG defines. SVGs with hardcoded colors (legacy diagrams) are converted as-is.

To flatten without converting (e.g. for another renderer):

```bash
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/flatten-vars.ts <svg-path> <output-path> [--theme=<name>]
```

## Process

1. Identify the diagram type; read its reference file if one exists
2. Plan the layout: list components, grouping and flow direction, calculate positions
3. Write the SVG in the layering order above, colors via CSS variables only, with the `:root { ... }` block using the dark defaults from the CSS Custom Properties table
4. Verify spacing rules — no overlaps, legends outside boundaries, viewBox large enough
5. Save as `<name>.svg` (the dark version)
6. Run `${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/theme-switch.ts <name>.svg --theme=light` → `<name>.light.svg`
7. Run `${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts <name>.svg` → `<name>@2x.png`
8. Run `${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts <name>.svg --theme light -o <name>.light@2x.png` → `<name>.light@2x.png`
9. Present the files listed in Output Files to the user

# Electron App Extract

## User Input Tools

When this skill prompts the user, follow this tool-selection rule (priority order):

1. **Prefer built-in user-input tools** exposed by the current agent runtime — e.g., `AskUserQuestion`, `request_user_input`, `clarify`, `ask_user`, or any equivalent.
2. **Fallback**: if no such tool exists, emit a numbered plain-text message and ask the user to reply with the chosen number/answer for each question.
3. **Batching**: if the tool supports multiple questions per call, combine all applicable questions into a single call; if only single-question, ask them one at a time in priority order.

Concrete `AskUserQuestion` references below are examples — substitute the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Script Directory

`{baseDir}` = this SKILL.md's directory. Resolve `${BUN_X}`: `bun` if installed; else `npx -y bun`; else suggest installing bun. Replace `{baseDir}` and `${BUN_X}` with actual values.

| Script            | Purpose                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `scripts/main.ts` | App discovery + asar extraction + source-map restoration + Prettier formatting |

## Workflow

**1. Determine the input.** Accepts an **app name** (e.g., `Codex`) or **absolute path** (`/Applications/Codex.app`, a `.asar` file, or a Windows install dir). Ask for it if not given; ask for a custom output directory if they want one.

**2. Run the script.**

```bash
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts "<app>" [--output <dir>] [--asar <path>] [--force]
```

If unsure discovery will find the right bundle, run with `--dry-run` first (prints resolved paths, writes nothing).

**3. Handle the result.**

- **Success** → report output paths and counts (extracted / restored / formatted).
- **Multiple matches** → script lists candidates and exits non-zero. Ask the user which one (via `AskUserQuestion` or the runtime equivalent), then re-run with the chosen absolute path.
- **Existing non-empty output dir** → script refuses without `--force`. Ask whether to overwrite (`--force`) or pick a new `--output`.
- **Unsupported platform / no match** → suggest `--asar /full/path/to/app.asar` if the user knows where the bundle lives.

**4. Point the user at the result** (default `~/Downloads/<AppName>-electron-extract/`):

- `restored/` exists → original source tree reconstructed from `.js.map` files; read this first.
- Only `extracted/` (no maps) → JS/CSS in `extracted/` was Prettier-formatted in place; read from there.

## Usage

```bash
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts Codex                                   # → ~/Downloads/Codex-electron-extract/
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts "/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app"  # .app bundle, install dir, or .asar
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts "C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Programs\codex"
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --asar /Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar Codex
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts Codex --output ~/work/codex-source
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts Codex --json                            # one JSON line on stdout
```

## Options

| Option           | Short | Description                                                     | Default                                  |
| ---------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `<app>`          |       | App name or absolute path. Required unless `--asar` is given.   | —                                        |
| `--output`       | `-o`  | Output directory                                                | `~/Downloads/<AppName>-electron-extract` |
| `--asar`         |       | Override the resolved `.asar` path                              | auto-discovered                          |
| `--force`        | `-f`  | Allow writing into a non-empty existing output dir              | false                                    |
| `--skip-format`  |       | Skip Prettier formatting                                        | false                                    |
| `--skip-restore` |       | Skip source-map restoration                                     | false                                    |
| `--no-unpacked`  |       | Don't copy `app.asar.unpacked/` alongside                       | false                                    |
| `--dry-run`      |       | Print resolved paths and exit without writing                   | false                                    |
| `--json`         |       | Emit one JSON-line summary on stdout (suppresses normal output) | false                                    |

## Output layout

```
~/Downloads/<AppName>-electron-extract/
├── extract-report.json          # JSON summary: counts, warnings, resolved paths
├── extracted/                   # raw asar contents (JS/CSS Prettier-formatted when no map)
│   └── ...                      # node_modules left untouched (skipped from format)
├── extracted.unpacked/          # copied from <asar>.unpacked/ if present
│   └── ...                      # native modules (.node), large assets
└── restored/                    # only present if at least one .js.map was usable
    └── <original/source/tree>   # rebuilt from sourcesContent in each .js.map
```

## Source-Map Path Restoration

Original source names and directory structure are preserved as far as the map allows:

- Each `sources[]` entry resolves with `sourceRoot` when present, then relative to the `.js.map` file's directory inside `extracted/` — e.g. `.vite/main/index.js.map` + `../../src/main.ts` → `restored/src/main.ts`.
- `../` segments are not treated as automatically unsafe: resolve from the map location first, then sanitize the final path so it stays under `restored/`. A path climbing above `extracted/` keeps its readable remainder — `.vite/main/index.js.map` + `../../../shared/src/lib/foo.ts` → `restored/shared/src/lib/foo.ts`.
- URL/query decorations are stripped (`webpack://`, `file://`, `?loader` suffixes).
- `restored/__unknown/<hash>.<ext>` only when the source name is empty or can't be reduced to a safe file path.
- `node_modules` and `webpack/runtime/*` entries are skipped (bundler/runtime noise).

## Notes

- **node_modules** is always skipped, for both source-map restoration and Prettier formatting.
- **Restoration needs embedded `sourcesContent`** (common for webpack, esbuild, Vite, rollup). Maps referencing external files without embedding them are skipped and the `.js` is Prettier-formatted instead; skipped maps appear in `extract-report.json` under `warnings`.
- **App discovery**: macOS `/Applications` + `~/Applications`; Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, `%PROGRAMFILES%`, `%PROGRAMFILES(X86)%`, `%APPDATA%`. Multiple matches → script exits and lists them; re-run with an absolute path. Linux/other: pass `--asar /path/to/app.asar`.
- **Safety**: refuses to write to `/`, the user home directly, or the current working directory, and refuses to populate an existing non-empty output dir without `--force`.
- **No global installs**: `@electron/asar` and `prettier` resolve on-the-fly via `npx -y`; first run is slower while npx caches them.

description: Formats plain text or markdown files with frontmatter, titles, summaries, headings, bold, lists, and code blocks. Use when user asks to "format markdown", "beautify article", "add formatting", or improve article layout. Outputs to {filename}-formatted.md.

# Markdown Formatter

Make plain text or markdown scannable so readers grasp key points and structure fast.

**Core principle**: Only adjust formatting and fix obvious typos. Never add, delete, or rewrite content.

## User Input Tools

When this skill prompts the user, follow this tool-selection rule (priority order):

1. **Prefer built-in user-input tools** exposed by the current agent runtime — e.g., `AskUserQuestion`, `request_user_input`, `clarify`, `ask_user`, or any equivalent.
2. **Fallback**: if no such tool exists, emit a numbered plain-text message and ask the user to reply with the chosen number/answer for each question.
3. **Batching**: if the tool supports multiple questions per call, combine all applicable questions into a single call; if only single-question, ask them one at a time in priority order.

Concrete `AskUserQuestion` references below are examples — substitute the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Script Directory

`{baseDir}` = this SKILL.md's directory. `${BUN_X}` = `bun` if installed; else `npx -y bun` if `npx` available; else suggest installing bun. Replace `{baseDir}` and `${BUN_X}` with actual values.

| Script | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `scripts/main.ts` | Main entry point with CLI options (uses remark-cjk-friendly for CJK emphasis) |
| `scripts/quotes.ts` | Replace ASCII quotes with fullwidth quotes |
| `scripts/autocorrect.ts` | Add CJK/English spacing via autocorrect |

## Preferences (EXTEND.md)

First one found wins:

| Priority | Path | Scope |
|----------|------|-------|
| 1 | `.baoyu-skills/baoyu-format-markdown/EXTEND.md` | Project |
| 2 | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/baoyu-skills/baoyu-format-markdown/EXTEND.md` | XDG |
| 3 | `$HOME/.baoyu-skills/baoyu-format-markdown/EXTEND.md` | User home |

None found → use defaults (no first-time setup for this skill).

| Setting | Values | Default | Description |
|---------|--------|---------|-------------|
| `auto_select` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Skip both title and summary selection, auto-pick best |
| `auto_select_title` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Skip title selection only |
| `auto_select_summary` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Skip summary selection only |
| Other | — | — | Default formatting options, typography preferences |

## Workflow

The agent analyzes and formats (Steps 1-5), then runs the typography script (Step 6).

### Step 1: Read & Detect Content Type

Read the file. It is **Markdown** if it has `---` YAML frontmatter, `#`/`##`/`###` headings, or `**bold**`/`*italic*`/lists/code blocks/blockquotes; otherwise **plain text**.

If Markdown, ask:

```
Detected existing markdown formatting. What would you like to do?

1. Optimize formatting (Recommended)
   - Analyze content, improve headings, bold, lists for readability
   - Run typography script (spacing, emphasis fixes)
   - Output: {filename}-formatted.md

2. Keep original formatting
   - Preserve existing markdown structure
   - Run typography script only
   - Output: {filename}-formatted.md

3. Typography fixes only
   - Run typography script on original file in-place
   - No copy created, modifies original file directly
```

- **Optimize** → Step 2 (full workflow)
- **Keep original** → skip to Step 5 (copy file), then Step 6
- **Typography only** → skip to Step 6 on the original file

### Step 2: Analyze Content (Reader's Perspective)

Read the whole text and ask what would help a reader quickly understand and remember it. Save `{original-filename}-analysis.md` — the blueprint for Step 4:

```markdown
# Content Analysis: {filename}

## Highlights & Key Insights
- [core arguments/conclusions, surprising facts or data, counterintuitive claims, golden quotes]

## Structure Assessment
- Current flow: [describe]
- Suggested sections: [heading candidates with brief rationale; unheaded section boundaries; walls of text needing breaks]

## Reader-Important Information
- [actionable takeaways, key definitions, lists buried in prose, comparisons that should be tables]

## Formatting Issues
- [specific issues with location: heading hierarchy, mixed-topic paragraphs, parallel items as prose, unmarked code/commands/terms]

## Typos Found
- [obvious typos with corrections, or "None found"]
```

### Step 3: Check/Create Frontmatter, Title & Summary

Create a YAML frontmatter block if missing.

| Field | Processing |
|-------|------------|
| `title` | See **Title Generation** |
| `slug` | Infer from file path or generate from title |
| `summary` | One-sentence summary (see **Summary Generation**) |
| `description` | Longer descriptive summary (see **Summary Generation**) |
| `coverImage` | If `imgs/cover.png` exists in the same directory, use its relative path |

#### Title Generation

Run this flow even if a title exists, unless `auto_select_title` is set.

1. Extract: core argument (one sentence), most impactful opinion/conclusion, reader pain point or curiosity trigger, most memorable metaphor or golden quote
2. Using [references/title-formulas.md](references/title-formulas.md): pick the **2-3 best-matching hook formulas** ("When to pick each formula"), plus **1-2 straightforward titles** (descriptive or declarative, no formula). If the user gave a direction (e.g., "make it suspenseful"), prioritize it. Total **4-5 candidates**, obeying the reference's principles and prohibited patterns
3. Ask, strongest hook first and marked `(recommended)`:

```
Pick a title:

1. [Hook title A] — (recommended) [formula name]
2. [Hook title B] — [formula name]
3. [Hook title C] — [formula name]
4. [Straightforward title D] — straightforward
5. [Straightforward title E] — straightforward

Enter number, or type a custom title:
```

- First line is an H1 → move it to frontmatter and remove it from the body. An existing frontmatter `title` is context only; still generate fresh candidates.
- `auto_select: true` or `auto_select_title: true` → skip the prompt, use the top candidate.
- Once the title is in frontmatter, the body must NOT contain an H1.

#### Summary Generation

Generate both directly (no user selection):

| Field | Length | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `summary` | 1 sentence, ~50-80 chars | Concise hook — feeds, social sharing, SEO meta |
| `description` | 2-3 sentences, ~100-200 chars | Richer context — article previews, newsletter blurbs |

- Convey **core value** to the reader, not just the topic; prefer concrete details (numbers, outcomes, specific methods)
- `summary` punchy and self-contained; `description` may add supporting details
- Keep an existing `summary`/`description`; only generate the missing one
- Prohibited: "This article introduces...", "This article explores..."; pure topic description without value; restating the title

### Step 4: Format Content

Guided by the Step 2 analysis, make content scannable and key points impossible to miss, using headings (`##`/`###`), bold, ordered/unordered lists, tables, inline/fenced code (commands, paths, technical terms), blockquotes, and `---` for major transitions.

**Don't:**
- Add sentences, explanations, or commentary
- Delete or shorten any content
- Rephrase or rewrite the author's words
- Add editorializing headings (e.g., "Amazing Discovery" — use neutral descriptive ones)
- Over-format: not every sentence needs bold, not every paragraph a heading

**Do:**
- Preserve the author's voice, tone, and every word
- **Bold key conclusions and core takeaways** — what a reader would highlight
- Turn prose into lists only when the parallel structure is clearly there
- Add headings where the topic genuinely shifts — vivid and specific over generic (e.g., "3 天搞定 vs 传统方案" over "方案对比")
- Tables for comparisons or structured data buried in prose
- Blockquotes for golden quotes, memorable statements, or important warnings
- Fix obvious typos (from Step 2)
- Specify the language on code blocks (e.g., `python`, `javascript`)
- Maintain CJK/English spacing standards

### Step 5: Save Formatted File

Save as `{original-filename}-formatted.md`, backing up any existing one:

```bash
if [ -f "{filename}-formatted.md" ]; then
  mv "{filename}-formatted.md" "{filename}-formatted.backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).md"
fi
```

### Step 6: Execute Typography Script

```bash
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts {output-file-path} [options]
```

| Option | Short | Description | Default |
|--------|-------|-------------|---------|
| `--quotes` | `-q` | Replace ASCII quotes with fullwidth quotes `"..."` | false |
| `--no-quotes` | | Do not replace quotes | |
| `--spacing` | `-s` | Add CJK/English spacing via autocorrect | true |
| `--no-spacing` | | Do not add CJK/English spacing | |
| `--emphasis` | `-e` | Fix CJK emphasis punctuation issues | true |
| `--no-emphasis` | | Do not fix CJK emphasis issues | |

Frontmatter YAML is always formatted. Examples: `main.ts article.md` (defaults), `--quotes` (add quote replacement), `--no-spacing` (emphasis only).

### Step 7: Completion Report

Report actual changes; omit categories with none:

```
**Formatting Complete**

**Files:**
- Analysis: {filename}-analysis.md
- Formatted: {filename}-formatted.md

**Content Analysis Summary:**
- Highlights found: X key insights
- Golden quotes: X memorable sentences
- Formatting issues fixed: X items

**Changes Applied:**
- Frontmatter: [added/updated] (title, slug, summary)
- Headings added: X (##: N, ###: N)
- Bold markers added: X
- Lists created: X (from prose → list conversion)
- Tables created: X
- Code markers added: X
- Blockquotes added: X
- Typos fixed: X [list each: "original" → "corrected"]

**Typography Script:**
- CJK spacing: [applied/skipped]
- Emphasis fixes: [applied/skipped]
- Quote replacement: [applied/skipped]
```

## Extension Support

Custom configurations via EXTEND.md — see **Preferences** above.

| `scripts/quotes.ts` | Replace ASCII quotes with fullwidth quotes |
| `scripts/autocorrect.ts` | Add CJK/English spacing via autocorrect |

## Preferences (EXTEND.md)

First one found wins:

| Priority | Path | Scope |
|----------|------|-------|
| 1 | `.baoyu-skills/baoyu-format-markdown/EXTEND.md` | Project |
| 2 | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/baoyu-skills/baoyu-format-markdown/EXTEND.md` | XDG |
| 3 | `$HOME/.baoyu-skills/baoyu-format-markdown/EXTEND.md` | User home |

None found → use defaults (no first-time setup for this skill).

| Setting | Values | Default | Description |
|---------|--------|---------|-------------|
| `auto_select` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Skip both title and summary selection, auto-pick best |
| `auto_select_title` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Skip title selection only |
| `auto_select_summary` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Skip summary selection only |
| Other | — | — | Default formatting options, typography preferences |

## Workflow

The agent analyzes and formats (Steps 1-5), then runs the typography script (Step 6).

### Step 1: Read & Detect Content Type

Read the file. It is **Markdown** if it has `---` YAML frontmatter, `#`/`##`/`###` headings, or `**bold**`/`*italic*`/lists/code blocks/blockquotes; otherwise **plain text**.

If Markdown, ask:

```
Detected existing markdown formatting. What would you like to do?

1. Optimize formatting (Recommended)
   - Analyze content, improve headings, bold, lists for readability
   - Run typography script (spacing, emphasis fixes)
   - Output: {filename}-formatted.md

2. Keep original formatting
   - Preserve existing markdown structure
   - Run typography script only
   - Output: {filename}-formatted.md

3. Typography fixes only
   - Run typography script on original file in-place
   - No copy created, modifies original file directly
```

- **Optimize** → Step 2 (full workflow)
- **Keep original** → skip to Step 5 (copy file), then Step 6
- **Typography only** → skip to Step 6 on the original file

### Step 2: Analyze Content (Reader's Perspective)

Read the whole text and ask what would help a reader quickly understand and remember it. Save `{original-filename}-analysis.md` — the blueprint for Step 4:

```markdown
# Content Analysis: {filename}

## Highlights & Key Insights
- [core arguments/conclusions, surprising facts or data, counterintuitive claims, golden quotes]

## Structure Assessment
- Current flow: [describe]
- Suggested sections: [heading candidates with brief rationale; unheaded section boundaries; walls of text needing breaks]

## Reader-Important Information
- [actionable takeaways, key definitions, lists buried in prose, comparisons that should be tables]

## Formatting Issues
- [specific issues with location: heading hierarchy, mixed-topic paragraphs, parallel items as prose, unmarked code/commands/terms]

## Typos Found
- [obvious typos with corrections, or "None found"]
```

### Step 3: Check/Create Frontmatter, Title & Summary

Create a YAML frontmatter block if missing.

| Field | Processing |
|-------|------------|
| `title` | See **Title Generation** |
| `slug` | Infer from file path or generate from title |
| `summary` | One-sentence summary (see **Summary Generation**) |
| `description` | Longer descriptive summary (see **Summary Generation**) |
| `coverImage` | If `imgs/cover.png` exists in the same directory, use its relative path |

#### Title Generation

Run this flow even if a title exists, unless `auto_select_title` is set.

1. Extract: core argument (one sentence), most impactful opinion/conclusion, reader pain point or curiosity trigger, most memorable metaphor or golden quote
2. Using [references/title-formulas.md](references/title-formulas.md): pick the **2-3 best-matching hook formulas** ("When to pick each formula"), plus **1-2 straightforward titles** (descriptive or declarative, no formula). If the user gave a direction (e.g., "make it suspenseful"), prioritize it. Total **4-5 candidates**, obeying the reference's principles and prohibited patterns
3. Ask, strongest hook first and marked `(recommended)`:

```
Pick a title:

1. [Hook title A] — (recommended) [formula name]
2. [Hook title B] — [formula name]
3. [Hook title C] — [formula name]
4. [Straightforward title D] — straightforward
5. [Straightforward title E] — straightforward

Enter number, or type a custom title:
```

- First line is an H1 → move it to frontmatter and remove it from the body. An existing frontmatter `title` is context only; still generate fresh candidates.
- `auto_select: true` or `auto_select_title: true` → skip the prompt, use the top candidate.
- Once the title is in frontmatter, the body must NOT contain an H1.

#### Summary Generation

Generate both directly (no user selection):

| Field | Length | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `summary` | 1 sentence, ~50-80 chars | Concise hook — feeds, social sharing, SEO meta |
| `description` | 2-3 sentences, ~100-200 chars | Richer context — article previews, newsletter blurbs |

- Convey **core value** to the reader, not just the topic; prefer concrete details (numbers, outcomes, specific methods)
- `summary` punchy and self-contained; `description` may add supporting details
- Keep an existing `summary`/`description`; only generate the missing one
- Prohibited: "This article introduces...", "This article explores..."; pure topic description without value; restating the title

### Step 4: Format Content

Guided by the Step 2 analysis, make content scannable and key points impossible to miss, using headings (`##`/`###`), bold, ordered/unordered lists, tables, inline/fenced code (commands, paths, technical terms), blockquotes, and `---` for major transitions.

**Don't:**
- Add sentences, explanations, or commentary
- Delete or shorten any content
- Rephrase or rewrite the author's words
- Add editorializing headings (e.g., "Amazing Discovery" — use neutral descriptive ones)
- Over-format: not every sentence needs bold, not every paragraph a heading

**Do:**
- Preserve the author's voice, tone, and every word
- **Bold key conclusions and core takeaways** — what a reader would highlight
- Turn prose into lists only when the parallel structure is clearly there
- Add headings where the topic genuinely shifts — vivid and specific over generic (e.g., "3 天搞定 vs 传统方案" over "方案对比")
- Tables for comparisons or structured data buried in prose
- Blockquotes for golden quotes, memorable statements, or important warnings
- Fix obvious typos (from Step 2)
- Specify the language on code blocks (e.g., `python`, `javascript`)
- Maintain CJK/English spacing standards

### Step 5: Save Formatted File

Save as `{original-filename}-formatted.md`, backing up any existing one:

```bash
if [ -f "{filename}-formatted.md" ]; then
  mv "{filename}-formatted.md" "{filename}-formatted.backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).md"
fi
```

### Step 6: Execute Typography Script

```bash
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts {output-file-path} [options]
```

| Option | Short | Description | Default |
|--------|-------|-------------|---------|
| `--quotes` | `-q` | Replace ASCII quotes with fullwidth quotes `"..."` | false |
| `--no-quotes` | | Do not replace quotes | |
| `--spacing` | `-s` | Add CJK/English spacing via autocorrect | true |
| `--no-spacing` | | Do not add CJK/English spacing | |
| `--emphasis` | `-e` | Fix CJK emphasis punctuation issues | true |
| `--no-emphasis` | | Do not fix CJK emphasis issues | |

Frontmatter YAML is always formatted. Examples: `main.ts article.md` (defaults), `--quotes` (add quote replacement), `--no-spacing` (emphasis only).

### Step 7: Completion Report

Report actual changes; omit categories with none:

```
**Formatting Complete**

**Files:**
- Analysis: {filename}-analysis.md
- Formatted: {filename}-formatted.md

**Content Analysis Summary:**
- Highlights found: X key insights
- Golden quotes: X memorable sentences
- Formatting issues fixed: X items

**Changes Applied:**
- Frontmatter: [added/updated] (title, slug, summary)
- Headings added: X (##: N, ###: N)
- Bold markers added: X
- Lists created: X (from prose → list conversion)
- Tables created: X
- Code markers added: X
- Blockquotes added: X
- Typos fixed: X [list each: "original" → "corrected"]

**Typography Script:**
- CJK spacing: [applied/skipped]
- Emphasis fixes: [applied/skipped]
- Quote replacement: [applied/skipped]
```

## Extension Support

Custom configurations via EXTEND.md — see **Preferences** above.

# Image Generation (AI SDK)

## User Input Tools

When this skill prompts the user, follow this tool-selection rule (priority order):

1. **Prefer built-in user-input tools** exposed by the current agent runtime — e.g., `AskUserQuestion`, `request_user_input`, `clarify`, `ask_user`, or any equivalent.
2. **Fallback**: if no such tool exists, emit a numbered plain-text message and ask the user to reply with the chosen number/answer for each question.
3. **Batching**: if the tool supports multiple questions per call, combine all applicable questions into a single call; if only single-question, ask them one at a time in priority order.

Concrete `AskUserQuestion` references below are examples — substitute the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Script Directory

`{baseDir}` = this SKILL.md's directory; `scripts/...` paths are relative to it. Main script: `{baseDir}/scripts/main.ts`. Batch payload helper: `{baseDir}/scripts/build-batch.ts`. Resolve `${BUN_X}`: prefer `bun`; else `npx -y bun`; else suggest `brew install oven-sh/bun/bun`.

## Step 0: Load Preferences (blocking)

No image generation until EXTEND.md exists. Check in order; first hit wins:

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.baoyu-skills/baoyu-image-gen/EXTEND.md` | Project |
| `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/baoyu-skills/baoyu-image-gen/EXTEND.md` | XDG |
| `$HOME/.baoyu-skills/baoyu-image-gen/EXTEND.md` | User home |

- **Found** → load and apply. If `default_model.[provider]` is null → ask model only.
- **Not found** → run first-time setup (`references/config/first-time-setup.md`) via AskUserQuestion to collect provider + model + quality + save location. Save EXTEND.md, then continue.

Legacy: if `.baoyu-skills/baoyu-imagine/EXTEND.md` exists and the new path doesn't, the runtime renames it to `baoyu-image-gen`. If both exist, the runtime leaves them alone and uses the new path.

**EXTEND.md keys**: default provider, quality, aspect ratio, image size, OpenAI image API dialect, default models, batch worker cap, provider-specific batch limits. Schema: `references/config/preferences-schema.md`.

## Usage

More examples (per provider, batch file format): `references/usage-examples.md`.

```bash
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --prompt "A cat" --image cat.png
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --prompt "A landscape" --image out.png --ar 16:9 --quality 2k
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --promptfiles system.md content.md --image out.png
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --prompt "Make blue" --image out.png --ref source.png
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --prompt "A cat" --image out.png --provider dashscope --model qwen-image-2.0-pro
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --prompt "A cat" --image out.png --provider codex-cli --ar 16:9   # Codex login, no OPENAI_API_KEY; needs `codex` on PATH

# Batch; build the payload from outline.md + prompts/ (e.g. baoyu-article-illustrator output)
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/build-batch.ts --outline outline.md --prompts prompts --output batch.json --images-dir attachments
${BUN_X} {baseDir}/scripts/main.ts --batchfile batch.json --jobs 4
```

## Reference-Image Identity Preservation

When a real person/character/object must be preserved from reference images:

- Use short, hard identity language instead of a long generic description: "Use the person/object in the reference image(s) as the same identity. Do not redesign it or create a similar-looking new subject. Only change scene, clothing, pose, lighting, rendering style, and composition. Keep the face/proportions/hair/key accessories/overall identity from the references." With multiple refs, say they are the same subject and jointly define identity.
- Long feature descriptions ("young East Asian woman, oval face, clear eyes...") make the model synthesize a new matching person instead.
- Prefer 2–4 curated existing source refs; many or multi-megabyte refs can destabilize streaming providers.
- Don't use newly generated outputs as refs unless the user asks (drift compounds).
- Too polished/influencer-like → reduce stylized refs, add anti-beautification constraints (no face slimming, eye enlargement, heavy makeup, commercial travel shoot, over-smoothing).
- Younger/older look → keep the face; express age via clothing, posture, scene, styling. Never ask to change facial identity.

## Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--prompt <text>`, `-p` | Prompt text |
| `--promptfiles <files...>` | Read prompt from files (concatenated) |
| `--image <path>` | Output image path (required in single-image mode) |
| `--batchfile <path>` | JSON batch file for multi-image generation |
| `--jobs <count>` | Worker count for batch mode (default: auto, max from config, built-in default 10) |
| `--provider google\|openai\|azure\|openrouter\|dashscope\|zai\|minimax\|jimeng\|seedream\|replicate\|codex-cli\|agnes` | Force provider (default: auto-detect; `codex-cli` is never auto-selected — must be pinned via CLI or EXTEND.md) |
| `--model <id>`, `-m` | Model ID — see provider references for defaults and allowed values |
| `--ar <ratio>` | Aspect ratio (`16:9`, `1:1`, `4:3`, …) |
| `--size <WxH>` | Explicit size (e.g., `1024x1024`; for `gpt-image-2.5-*` and `gpt-image-2`, width/height must be multiples of 16, max edge 3840px, ratio no wider than 3:1) |
| `--quality normal\|2k` | Quality preset (default: `2k`) |
| `--imageSize 1K\|2K\|4K` | Image size for Google/OpenRouter (default: from quality) |
| `--imageApiDialect openai-native\|ratio-metadata` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint dialect — use `ratio-metadata` for gateways that expect aspect-ratio `size` plus `metadata.resolution` |
| `--ref <files...>` | Reference images. Supported by Google multimodal, OpenAI GPT Image edits, Azure OpenAI edits (PNG/JPG only), OpenRouter multimodal models, Replicate supported families, MiniMax subject-reference, Seedream 5.0/4.5/4.0, DashScope `wan2.7-image-pro`/`wan2.7-image`. Not supported by Jimeng, Seedream 3.0, SeedEdit 3.0, or any DashScope model outside the `wan2.7-image*` family |
| `--n <count>` | Number of images. Replicate requires `--n 1` (single-output save semantics) |
| `--json` | JSON output |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key |
| `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` | Azure OpenAI API key |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter API key |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Google API key |
| `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` | DashScope API key |
| `ZAI_API_KEY` (alias `BIGMODEL_API_KEY`) | Z.AI API key |
| `MINIMAX_API_KEY` | MiniMax API key |
| `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN` | Replicate API token |
| `JIMENG_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `JIMENG_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Jimeng (即梦) Volcengine credentials |
| `ARK_API_KEY` | Seedream (豆包) Volcengine ARK API key |
| `<PROVIDER>_IMAGE_MODEL` | Per-provider model override (`OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL`, `GOOGLE_IMAGE_MODEL`, `DASHSCOPE_IMAGE_MODEL`, `ZAI_IMAGE_MODEL`/`BIGMODEL_IMAGE_MODEL`, `MINIMAX_IMAGE_MODEL`, `OPENROUTER_IMAGE_MODEL`, `REPLICATE_IMAGE_MODEL`, `JIMENG_IMAGE_MODEL`, `SEEDREAM_IMAGE_MODEL`, `AGNES_IMAGE_MODEL`) |
| `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT` (alias `AZURE_OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL`) | Azure default deployment |
| `<PROVIDER>_BASE_URL` | Per-provider endpoint override |
| `AZURE_API_VERSION` | Azure image API version (default `2025-04-01-preview`) |
| `JIMENG_REGION` | Jimeng region (default `cn-north-1`) |
| `OPENAI_IMAGE_API_DIALECT` | `openai-native` \| `ratio-metadata` |
| `OPENROUTER_HTTP_REFERER`, `OPENROUTER_TITLE` | Optional OpenRouter attribution |
| `BAOYU_IMAGE_GEN_MAX_WORKERS` | Override batch worker cap |
| `BAOYU_IMAGE_GEN_<PROVIDER>_CONCURRENCY` | Per-provider concurrency (e.g., `BAOYU_IMAGE_GEN_REPLICATE_CONCURRENCY`; for codex-cli use `BAOYU_IMAGE_GEN_CODEX_CLI_CONCURRENCY`) |
| `BAOYU_IMAGE_GEN_<PROVIDER>_START_INTERVAL_MS` | Per-provider start-gap |
| `BAOYU_CODEX_IMAGEGEN_BIN` | Override the codex-imagegen wrapper path for the `codex-cli` provider (default: bundled `scripts/codex-imagegen/main.ts`; accepts `.ts` or legacy `.sh`/binary) |
| `BAOYU_CODEX_IMAGEGEN_CACHE_DIR` | Enable idempotency cache for the `codex-cli` provider (off by default) |
| `BAOYU_CODEX_IMAGEGEN_TIMEOUT_MS` | Per-attempt `codex exec` timeout for the `codex-cli` provider (default: 300000 ms) |
| `BAOYU_CODEX_IMAGEGEN_RETRIES` | Wrapper-side retry attempts on retryable errors for the `codex-cli` provider (default: 2) |
| `BAOYU_CODEX_IMAGEGEN_LOG_FILE` | Append JSONL diagnostic log for the `codex-cli` provider |

**Load priority**: CLI args > EXTEND.md > env vars > `<cwd>/.baoyu-skills/.env` > `~/.baoyu-skills/.env`

## Codex/ChatGPT OAuth Is Not an OpenAI API Key

`--provider openai` calls the standard OpenAI Images API (`/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`) and requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. A Codex/ChatGPT login is a different entitlement: never paste a Codex OAuth token into `OPENAI_API_KEY` or just point `OPENAI_BASE_URL` at a Codex backend. Do not modify the `openai` provider to silently consume Codex OAuth.

To use a Codex subscription without an API key:

- Codex runtime: native `imagegen` skill/tool.
- Non-Codex runtime with `codex` CLI installed and logged in: `--provider codex-cli` (preferred; same retry/cache/batch flow). It spawns the bundled `scripts/codex-imagegen/main.ts` (upstream: `packages/baoyu-codex-imagegen/src/main.ts`).
- Hermes runtime with native `image_generate`: use as fallback; state whether refs were passed directly or reconstructed from extracted traits.

**Fallback**: if `--provider openai` fails only because `OPENAI_API_KEY` is missing and one of the backends above is available, use it rather than leaving the user waiting, and say whether it was true reference-image generation or a text reconstruction from visual traits. Details: `references/codex-oauth-vs-openai-api-key.md`, `references/codex-image2-fallback.md`.

## Model Resolution

Priority for every provider: CLI `--model <id>` > EXTEND.md `default_model.[provider]` > env `<PROVIDER>_IMAGE_MODEL` > built-in default.

- **OpenAI**: default `gpt-image-2.5-flare` (fastest). `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` is most capable for complex scenes and precise edits; `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-1` and dated snapshots (e.g. `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`) stay selectable.
- **Google**: default `gemini-3-pro-image`. `gemini-3.1-flash-image` is faster/cheaper; `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` is cheapest and 1K-only (`--quality 2k` / `--imageSize 2K|4K` clamp to 1K with a warning).
- **DashScope**: default `qwen-image-2.0-pro`; `qwen-image-3.0-pro` is the newest flagship with the same sizing rules.
- **Azure**: `--model` / `default_model.azure` is the deployment name (`AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT`, alias `AZURE_OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL`). Use `gpt-image-2.5-flare` if the deployment is named after the model, else the exact custom name.

Before each generation, display:

- `Using [provider] / [model]`
- `Switch model: --model <id> | EXTEND.md default_model.[provider] | env <PROVIDER>_IMAGE_MODEL`

## OpenAI-Compatible Gateway Dialects

`provider=openai` only means OpenAI-compatible auth/routing, not native image semantics. Set `default_image_api_dialect` (EXTEND.md), `OPENAI_IMAGE_API_DIALECT`, or `--imageApiDialect`:

- `openai-native`: pixel `size` (`1536x1024`) and native quality fields — OpenAI and strict clones
- `ratio-metadata`: aspect-ratio `size` (`16:9`) + `metadata.resolution` (`1K|2K|4K`) + `metadata.orientation` — gateways fronting Gemini or similar. Text-to-image only; reference edits need `openai-native` or a provider with first-class edit support.

## Provider-Specific Guides

Read when the user picks that provider or asks for non-default behavior:

| Provider | Reference |
|----------|-----------|
| DashScope (Qwen-Image families, custom sizes) | `references/providers/dashscope.md` |
| Z.AI (GLM-Image, cogview-4) | `references/providers/zai.md` |
| MiniMax (image-01, subject-reference) | `references/providers/minimax.md` |
| OpenRouter (multimodal models, `/chat/completions` flow) | `references/providers/openrouter.md` |
| Replicate (nano-banana, Seedream, Wan) | `references/providers/replicate.md` |
| Codex CLI (wraps bundled `scripts/codex-imagegen/`; Codex login, no `OPENAI_API_KEY`) | `references/providers/codex-cli.md` |
| Agnes (agnes-image-2.5-flash, reference-image support) | `references/providers/agnes.md` |

## Provider Selection

1. `--ref` provided + no `--provider` → auto-select Google → OpenAI → Azure → OpenRouter → Replicate → Seedream → MiniMax → Agnes (MiniMax subject reference is specialized for character/portrait consistency)
2. `--provider` specified → use it (with `--ref`, must be google/openai/azure/openrouter/replicate/seedream/minimax/codex-cli/agnes)
3. Only one API key present → that provider
4. Multiple keys → Google → OpenAI → Azure → OpenRouter → DashScope → Z.AI → MiniMax → Replicate → Jimeng → Seedream → Agnes
5. `codex-cli` is **never auto-selected** — pin via `default_provider: codex-cli` or `--provider codex-cli`. Runs `codex exec` through the bundled `scripts/codex-imagegen/main.ts` (with `bun`) on the user's Codex subscription; requires `codex` on `PATH` with an active `codex login`.

## Quality Presets

| Preset | Google imageSize | OpenAI size | OpenRouter size | Replicate resolution | Use case |
|--------|------------------|-------------|-----------------|----------------------|----------|
| `normal` | 1K | 1024px target | 1K | 1K | Quick previews |
| `2k` (default) | 2K | 2048px target | 2K | 2K | Covers, illustrations, infographics |

Google/OpenRouter `imageSize` can be overridden with `--imageSize 1K|2K|4K`.

OpenAI native `gpt-image-2.5-*` / `gpt-image-2`: `normal` → `quality=medium` + low-latency valid size near the ratio; `2k` → `quality=high` + 2048px-class sizes (`2048x2048`, `2048x1152`, `1152x2048`). Use explicit `--size` for custom or 4K (e.g. `3840x2160`).

## Aspect Ratios

Supported: `1:1`, `16:9`, `9:16`, `4:3`, `3:4`, `2.35:1`.

- Google multimodal: `imageConfig.aspectRatio`
- OpenAI: `gpt-image-2.5-*` / `gpt-image-2` use the closest valid custom size; older GPT Image and DALL·E use the closest fixed size
- OpenRouter: `imageGenerationOptions.aspect_ratio`; with only `--size <WxH>`, the ratio is inferred
- Replicate: model-specific — `google/nano-banana*` uses `aspect_ratio`, `bytedance/seedream-*` uses documented Replicate ratios, Wan 2.7 maps `--ar` to a concrete `size`
- MiniMax: official `aspect_ratio` values; `--size <WxH>` without `--ar` sends `width`/`height` for `image-01`

## Generation Mode

**Default**: sequential. **Batch parallel**: automatic when `--batchfile` has 2+ pending tasks.

| Situation | Prefer |
|-----------|--------|
| One image, or 1-2 simple images | Sequential |
| Multiple images with saved prompt files | Batch (`--batchfile`) — shared throttling/retries |
| Each image still needs its own reasoning / prompt writing / style exploration | Subagents |
| Input is `outline.md` + `prompts/` (e.g. from `baoyu-article-illustrator`) | Batch, payload built with `{baseDir}/scripts/build-batch.ts` |

Once prompt files are saved and the task is "generate all of these", prefer batch over subagents.

**Parallel behavior**: worker count auto, capped by config (built-in default 10), override with `--jobs <count>`; provider-specific throttling applies only in batch mode; each image retries up to 3 attempts; final output reports success count, failure count, and per-image failure reasons.

## Error Handling

- Missing API key → error with setup instructions (for OpenAI see the Codex fallback above)
- Generation failure → auto-retry up to 3 attempts per image
- Invalid aspect ratio → warning, proceed with default
- Reference images with unsupported provider/model → error with fix hint

## Extension Support

Custom configurations via EXTEND.md. See Step 0 for paths and schema.

# Image Generation (AI SDK)

## User Input Tools

When this skill prompts the user, follow this tool-selection rule (priority order):

1. **Prefer built-in user-input tools** exposed by the current agent runtime — e.g., `AskUserQuestion`, `request_user_input`, `clarify`, `ask_user`, or any equivalent.
2. **Fallback**: if no such tool exists, emit a numbered plain-text message and ask the user to reply with the chosen number/answer for each question.
3. **Batching**: if the tool supports multiple questions per call, combine all applicable questions into a single call; if only single-question, ask them one at a time in priority order.

Concrete `AskUserQuestion` references below are examples — substitute the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Script Directory

`{baseDir}` = this SKILL.md's directory; `scripts/...` paths are relative to it. Main script: `{baseDir}/scripts/main.ts`. Batch payload helper: `{baseDir}/scripts/build-batch.ts`. Resolve `${BUN_X}`: prefer `bun`; else `npx -y bun`; else suggest `brew install oven-sh/bun/bun`.

## Reference-Image Identity Preservation

When a real person/character/object must be preserved from reference images:

- Use short, hard identity language instead of a long generic description: "Use the person/object in the reference image(s) as the same identity. Do not redesign it or create a similar-looking new subject. Only change scene, clothing, pose, lighting, rendering style, and composition. Keep the face/proportions/hair/key accessories/overall identity from the references." With multiple refs, say they are the same subject and jointly define identity.
- Long feature descriptions ("young East Asian woman, oval face, clear eyes...") make the model synthesize a new matching person instead.
- Prefer 2–4 curated existing source refs; many or multi-megabyte refs can destabilize streaming providers.
- Don't use newly generated outputs as refs unless the user asks (drift compounds).
- Too polished/influencer-like → reduce stylized refs, add anti-beautification constraints (no face slimming, eye enlargement, heavy makeup, commercial travel shoot, over-smoothing).
- Younger/older look → keep the face; express age via clothing, posture, scene, styling. Never ask to change facial identity.

## Codex/ChatGPT OAuth Is Not an OpenAI API Key

`--provider openai` calls the standard OpenAI Images API (`/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`) and requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. A Codex/ChatGPT login is a different entitlement: never paste a Codex OAuth token into `OPENAI_API_KEY` or just point `OPENAI_BASE_URL` at a Codex backend. Do not modify the `openai` provider to silently consume Codex OAuth.

To use a Codex subscription without an API key:

- Codex runtime: native `imagegen` skill/tool.
- Non-Codex runtime with `codex` CLI installed and logged in: `--provider codex-cli` (preferred; same retry/cache/batch flow). It spawns the bundled `scripts/codex-imagegen/main.ts` (upstream: `packages/baoyu-codex-imagegen/src/main.ts`).
- Hermes runtime with native `image_generate`: use as fallback; state whether refs were passed directly or reconstructed from extracted traits.

**Fallback**: if `--provider openai` fails only because `OPENAI_API_KEY` is missing and one of the backends above is available, use it rather than leaving the user waiting, and say whether it was true reference-image generation or a text reconstruction from visual traits. Details: `references/codex-oauth-vs-openai-api-key.md`, `references/codex-image2-fallback.md`.

## Model Resolution

Priority for every provider: CLI `--model <id>` > EXTEND.md `default_model.[provider]` > env `<PROVIDER>_IMAGE_MODEL` > built-in default.

- **OpenAI**: default `gpt-image-2.5-flare` (fastest). `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` is most capable for complex scenes and precise edits; `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-1` and dated snapshots (e.g. `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`) stay selectable.
- **Google**: default `gemini-3-pro-image`. `gemini-3.1-flash-image` is faster/cheaper; `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` is cheapest and 1K-only (`--quality 2k` / `--imageSize 2K|4K` clamp to 1K with a warning).
- **DashScope**: default `qwen-image-2.0-pro`; `qwen-image-3.0-pro` is the newest flagship with the same sizing rules.
- **Azure**: `--model` / `default_model.azure` is the deployment name (`AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT`, alias `AZURE_OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL`). Use `gpt-image-2.5-flare` if the deployment is named after the model, else the exact custom name.

Before each generation, display:

- `Using [provider] / [model]`
- `Switch model: --model <id> | EXTEND.md default_model.[provider] | env <PROVIDER>_IMAGE_MODEL`

## OpenAI-Compatible Gateway Dialects

`provider=openai` only means OpenAI-compatible auth/routing, not native image semantics. Set `default_image_api_dialect` (EXTEND.md), `OPENAI_IMAGE_API_DIALECT`, or `--imageApiDialect`:

- `openai-native`: pixel `size` (`1536x1024`) and native quality fields — OpenAI and strict clones
- `ratio-metadata`: aspect-ratio `size` (`16:9`) + `metadata.resolution` (`1K|2K|4K`) + `metadata.orientation` — gateways fronting Gemini or similar. Text-to-image only; reference edits need `openai-native` or a provider with first-class edit support.

## Provider Selection

1. `--ref` provided + no `--provider` → auto-select Google → OpenAI → Azure → OpenRouter → Replicate → Seedream → MiniMax → Agnes (MiniMax subject reference is specialized for character/portrait consistency)
2. `--provider` specified → use it (with `--ref`, must be google/openai/azure/openrouter/replicate/seedream/minimax/codex-cli/agnes)
3. Only one API key present → that provider
4. Multiple keys → Google → OpenAI → Azure → OpenRouter → DashScope → Z.AI → MiniMax → Replicate → Jimeng → Seedream → Agnes
5. `codex-cli` is **never auto-selected** — pin via `default_provider: codex-cli` or `--provider codex-cli`. Runs `codex exec` through the bundled `scripts/codex-imagegen/main.ts` (with `bun`) on the user's Codex subscription; requires `codex` on `PATH` with an active `codex login`.

## Quality Presets

| Preset | Google imageSize | OpenAI size | OpenRouter size | Replicate resolution | Use case |
|--------|------------------|-------------|-----------------|----------------------|----------|
| `normal` | 1K | 1024px target | 1K | 1K | Quick previews |
| `2k` (default) | 2K | 2048px target | 2K | 2K | Covers, illustrations, infographics |

Google/OpenRouter `imageSize` can be overridden with `--imageSize 1K|2K|4K`.

OpenAI native `gpt-image-2.5-*` / `gpt-image-2`: `normal` → `quality=medium` + low-latency valid size near the ratio; `2k` → `quality=high` + 2048px-class sizes (`2048x2048`, `2048x1152`, `1152x2048`). Use explicit `--size` for custom or 4K (e.g. `3840x2160`).

## Aspect Ratios

Supported: `1:1`, `16:9`, `9:16`, `4:3`, `3:4`, `2.35:1`.

- Google multimodal: `imageConfig.aspectRatio`
- OpenAI: `gpt-image-2.5-*` / `gpt-image-2` use the closest valid custom size; older GPT Image and DALL·E use the closest fixed size
- OpenRouter: `imageGenerationOptions.aspect_ratio`; with only `--size <WxH>`, the ratio is inferred
- Replicate: model-specific — `google/nano-banana*` uses `aspect_ratio`, `bytedance/seedream-*` uses documented Replicate ratios, Wan 2.7 maps `--ar` to a concrete `size`
- MiniMax: official `aspect_ratio` values; `--size <WxH>` without `--ar` sends `width`/`height` for `image-01`

## Generation Mode

**Default**: sequential. **Batch parallel**: automatic when `--batchfile` has 2+ pending tasks.

| Situation | Prefer |
|-----------|--------|
| One image, or 1-2 simple images | Sequential |
| Multiple images with saved prompt files | Batch (`--batchfile`) — shared throttling/retries |
| Each image still needs its own reasoning / prompt writing / style exploration | Subagents |
| Input is `outline.md` + `prompts/` (e.g. from `baoyu-article-illustrator`) | Batch, payload built with `{baseDir}/scripts/build-batch.ts` |

Once prompt files are saved and the task is "generate all of these", prefer batch over subagents.

**Parallel behavior**: worker count auto, capped by config (built-in default 10), override with `--jobs <count>`; provider-specific throttling applies only in batch mode; each image retries up to 3 attempts; final output reports success count, failure count, and per-image failure reasons.

## Error Handling

- Missing API key → error with setup instructions (for OpenAI see the Codex fallback above)
- Generation failure → auto-retry up to 3 attempts per image
- Invalid aspect ratio → warning, proceed with default
- Reference images with unsupported provider/model → error with fix hint

2. **Fallback**: if no such tool exists, emit a numbered plain-text message and ask the user to reply with the chosen number/answer for each question.

## Image Generation Tools

Resolve the image backend in this order:

1. **User names a backend** in the current message → use it.
2. **`preferred_image_backend`** in `EXTEND.md` names a backend available now → use it. `ask` means ask every run.
3. **Auto-select** (preference `auto`, unset, or the pinned backend is unavailable), first match wins:
   - **Codex `imagegen`** skill is in your available skills → you are in Codex and MUST use it: `Skill` with `skill: "imagegen"`, passing the prompt file's content plus output path and aspect ratio. It outranks non-native skills such as `baoyu-image-gen`.
   - **Codex via `codex exec` (`codex-imagegen`)**: no native `imagegen`, but the `codex` CLI is on `PATH` with an active `codex login` → `baoyu-image-gen --provider codex-cli` (preferred), or the bundled wrapper if baoyu-image-gen is unavailable. Load [references/codex-imagegen.md](references/codex-imagegen.md) only for this branch.
   - **Cursor `GenerateImage`** → use it (outranks non-native skills). It has no aspect-ratio parameter, so state the aspect ratio / dimensions in the `description` prompt; it saves to a tool-managed location, so copy the file to the expected output path (e.g., `outputs/.../NN-xxx.png`). Reference images go in `reference_image_paths`.
   - **Other runtime-native image tool** (e.g., Hermes `image_generate`) → use it the same way.
   - Exactly one non-native backend installed (e.g., `baoyu-image-gen`) → use it.
   - Several non-native backends → ask the user once, batched with other initial questions.
4. **None available** → tell the user and ask how to proceed.

**⛔ Raster only**: never substitute SVG, HTML/CSS, canvas, or other code-based rendering for a raster image, even for diagram-like content. If no raster backend resolves, go to step 4.

**⛔ No bitmap text patching**: never use ImageMagick, Pillow, Canvas, SVG, HTML/CSS, OCR scripts, or any other overlay to cover, rewrite, erase, stroke, or replace labels, headings, callouts, data values, or any other text inside an already generated infographic. Regenerate from a corrected prompt, switch to a layout with less on-image text, or ask the user which imperfect candidate to keep.

**Prompt file (hard)**: before invoking any backend, write each image's full, final prompt to its own file under `prompts/` (`NN-{type}-[slug].md`) and pass that file (or its content) to the backend. It is the reproducibility record and lets you switch backends without rewriting prompts.

Change the pinned backend via `## Changing Preferences` below. Tool names above are examples; use the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Reference Images

Accept via `--ref <files...>`, file paths, or pasted images (guide style, palette, composition, or subject):
- File path(s) → copy to `refs/NN-ref-{slug}.{ext}` alongside the output
- Pasted image with no path → ask for the path (per User Input Tools), or extract style traits verbally as a text fallback

| Usage | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `direct` | Pass the file to the backend as a reference image |
| `style` | Extract style traits (line treatment, texture, mood) and append to the prompt body |
| `palette` | Extract hex colors from the image and append to the prompt body |

Record refs in `prompts/infographic.md` frontmatter:

```yaml
references:
  - ref_id: 01
    filename: 01-ref-brand.png
    usage: direct
```

At generation: verify each referenced file exists; if `usage: direct` AND the backend accepts reference images (e.g., `baoyu-image-gen` via `--ref`), pass it via the backend's ref parameter; otherwise embed extracted `style`/`palette` traits in the prompt text.

## Confirmation Policy

Default: **confirm before generation**.

- Explicit skill invocation, a file path, a matched keyword shortcut, `EXTEND.md` defaults, and the documented default combination are recommendation inputs only — none authorizes skipping confirmation.
- Do not start Step 5 or Step 6 until the user confirms the combination/aspect/language/backend choices.
- Skip confirmation only when the current request explicitly says so: `--no-confirm`, "直接生成", "不用确认", "跳过确认", "按默认出图", or equivalent. Then state the assumed combination/aspect/language/backend in the next user-facing update before generating.

# Infographic Generator

Two dimensions: **layout** (information structure) × **style** (visual aesthetics); any layout combines with any style.

## User Input Tools

When this skill prompts the user, follow this tool-selection rule (priority order):

1. **Prefer built-in user-input tools** exposed by the current agent runtime — e.g., `AskUserQuestion`, `request_user_input`, `clarify`, `ask_user`, or any equivalent.
2. **Fallback**: if no such tool exists, emit a numbered plain-text message and ask the user to reply with the chosen number/answer for each question.
3. **Batching**: if the tool supports multiple questions per call, combine all applicable questions into a single call; if only single-question, ask them one at a time in priority order.

Concrete `AskUserQuestion` references below are examples — substitute the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Image Generation Tools

Resolve the image backend in this order:

1. **User names a backend** in the current message → use it.
2. **`preferred_image_backend`** in `EXTEND.md` names a backend available now → use it. `ask` means ask every run.
3. **Auto-select** (preference `auto`, unset, or the pinned backend is unavailable), first match wins:
   - **Codex `imagegen`** skill is in your available skills → you are in Codex and MUST use it: `Skill` with `skill: "imagegen"`, passing the prompt file's content plus output path and aspect ratio. It outranks non-native skills such as `baoyu-image-gen`.
   - **Codex via `codex exec` (`codex-imagegen`)**: no native `imagegen`, but the `codex` CLI is on `PATH` with an active `codex login` → `baoyu-image-gen --provider codex-cli` (preferred), or the bundled wrapper if baoyu-image-gen is unavailable. Load [references/codex-imagegen.md](references/codex-imagegen.md) only for this branch.
   - **Cursor `GenerateImage`** → use it (outranks non-native skills). It has no aspect-ratio parameter, so state the aspect ratio / dimensions in the `description` prompt; it saves to a tool-managed location, so copy the file to the expected output path (e.g., `outputs/.../NN-xxx.png`). Reference images go in `reference_image_paths`.
   - **Other runtime-native image tool** (e.g., Hermes `image_generate`) → use it the same way.
   - Exactly one non-native backend installed (e.g., `baoyu-image-gen`) → use it.
   - Several non-native backends → ask the user once, batched with other initial questions.
4. **None available** → tell the user and ask how to proceed.

**⛔ Raster only**: never substitute SVG, HTML/CSS, canvas, or other code-based rendering for a raster image, even for diagram-like content. If no raster backend resolves, go to step 4.

**⛔ No bitmap text patching**: never use ImageMagick, Pillow, Canvas, SVG, HTML/CSS, OCR scripts, or any other overlay to cover, rewrite, erase, stroke, or replace labels, headings, callouts, data values, or any other text inside an already generated infographic. Regenerate from a corrected prompt, switch to a layout with less on-image text, or ask the user which imperfect candidate to keep.

**Prompt file (hard)**: before invoking any backend, write each image's full, final prompt to its own file under `prompts/` (`NN-{type}-[slug].md`) and pass that file (or its content) to the backend. It is the reproducibility record and lets you switch backends without rewriting prompts.

Change the pinned backend via `## Changing Preferences` below. Tool names above are examples; use the local equivalent in other runtimes.

## Reference Images

Accept via `--ref <files...>`, file paths, or pasted images (guide style, palette, composition, or subject):
- File path(s) → copy to `refs/NN-ref-{slug}.{ext}` alongside the output
- Pasted image with no path → ask for the path (per User Input Tools), or extract style traits verbally as a text fallback

| Usage | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `direct` | Pass the file to the backend as a reference image |
| `style` | Extract style traits (line treatment, texture, mood) and append to the prompt body |
| `palette` | Extract hex colors from the image and append to the prompt body |

Record refs in `prompts/infographic.md` frontmatter:

```yaml
references:
  - ref_id: 01
    filename: 01-ref-brand.png
    usage: direct
```

At generation: verify each referenced file exists; if `usage: direct` AND the backend accepts reference images (e.g., `baoyu-image-gen` via `--ref`), pass it via the backend's ref parameter; otherwise embed extracted `style`/`palette` traits in the prompt text.

## Confirmation Policy

Default: **confirm before generation**.

- Explicit skill invocation, a file path, a matched keyword shortcut, `EXTEND.md` defaults, and the documented default combination are recommendation inputs only — none authorizes skipping confirmation.
- Do not start Step 5 or Step 6 until the user confirms the combination/aspect/language/backend choices.
- Skip confirmation only when the current request explicitly says so: `--no-confirm`, "直接生成", "不用确认", "跳过确认", "按默认出图", or equivalent. Then state the assumed combination/aspect/language/backend in the next user-facing update before generating.

skills.desc: Posts content to WeChat Official Account (微信公众号) via API or Chrome CDP. Supports article posting (文章) with HTML, markdown, or plain text input, and image-text posting (贴图, formerly 图文) with multiple images.
